content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1: overtime for 8 general agents, chat deflection on both queues and 2 agents lent from payments. Predicted 80.7% service level for 18:15-20:00 at ₹1,260.","why":"The FD special-rate email (MKT-2026-556) is driving general calls 20–45% over forecast, with new-offer enquiries at 2.74x normal. Payments is a separate problem: it is about 4 agents short of plan because of sickness. Doing nothing leaves the window at 66.8%, with general at 61.3% and 9.0% abandons. R1 is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target within policy. General is predicted at 74.5% and payments at 88.6%, with abandons down to 5.2%. The rest-of-day figure is the same, 80.7%. No escalation is needed.","trade_offs":["Cost: R1 costs ₹1,260. R2 also reaches the target (80.1%) but costs more at ₹1,350, and leaves general lower at 72.1%. The cheaper plans all miss 80%: P3 reaches 71.8% at ₹564, P2 69.1% at ₹204, and P1 63.6% at no cost.","Customer impact: general still sits below target at 74.5% even under R1. The overall figure gets past 80% mainly because payments is strong at 88.6%. R1 also drops the general IVR callback, so callers wait in queue or are offered chat instead.","Risk to payments: lending 2 cross-skilled agents to general from 18:15 to 19:00 takes cover from a queue that is already short-staffed. The model still predicts payments at 88.6%, helped by chat deflection on payment-status and refund-status calls. R2 avoids moving anyone and keeps payments at 90.2%, but costs more."],"watch":"Check general's service level after 18:45. If too few of the 8 agents accept overtime, or chat uptake falls below 20%, general will stay well short of target and the plan is unlikely to reach 80% overall. Also watch payments between 18:15 and 19:00 while the 2 agents are lent out. Bring them back early if payments drops toward its current 25% level."}
